title: Kilmainham Gaol
geometryBasis: Named enclosure, mapped entrance forecourt and rear prison multipolygon including the west court. Public architectural reports distinguish the original gates and expanded Victorian east wing.
sectionBasis: The national record gives the 1796 sedimentary-stone buildings and a later three-storey east wing. The museum describes variable boundary height of 30–50 feet. The Qualla court image shows the stone wall, gate and ground memorial detail. The Overture building estimate is 16.21 m for the rear blocks, providing a check on the Victorian east wing ridge.
limitations: The outer wall and connected building silhouettes are tied to current map data. Roof pitches, wall height transitions, internal bay alignment, and smaller openings are estimated from the architectural inventory and the story photograph.
The former courthouse is a separate neighbor and interiors are outside the exterior model.
